title: Balance Sheet Reconciliation: What It Is and How to Do It
summary: What balance sheet reconciliation is, the step-by-step process, the accounts it covers, common pitfalls, and how AI agents automate it.
body_markdown:
The balance sheet is only as trustworthy as the reconciliations behind it. **Balance sheet reconciliation** is the process of verifying that every account on the balance sheet, cash, receivables, payables, accruals, and the rest, matches its supporting documentation. It is one of the most important controls in accounting, because it is how errors, omissions, and fraud get caught before the financial statements go out.


This guide explains what balance sheet reconciliation is, the step-by-step process, the accounts it covers, common pitfalls, and how AI agents automate it.


## **What is balance sheet reconciliation?**


Balance sheet reconciliation is the process of comparing the balances in a company's general ledger balance-sheet accounts to independent supporting evidence, bank statements, subledgers, schedules, and other documentation, to confirm they agree. Where they do not, the difference is investigated and resolved with an adjusting entry. It is a core part of the[month-end close](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/month-end-close-process) and a key internal control.


> Balance sheet reconciliation answers one question for every account: can we prove this balance is right? If the number in the ledger does not tie to independent evidence, it is not yet trustworthy.


## **Balance sheet reconciliation vs. account reconciliation**


The terms overlap. **Account reconciliation** is the general practice of reconciling any account; **balance sheet reconciliation** specifically means reconciling the balance-sheet accounts (assets, liabilities, and equity) as a group, which is the heart of the close. Bank reconciliation is one specific type within it. For the broader category and tools, see[account reconciliation software](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/best-account-reconciliation-software) .


## **The balance sheet reconciliation process**


- **1. Pull the GL balance.** Get the ending balance for each balance-sheet account from the general ledger.
- **2. Gather supporting evidence.** Collect the independent documentation: bank statements, subledger reports, amortization schedules, loan statements, and so on.
- **3. Compare and match.** Compare the GL balance to the supporting total and match the detail.
- **4. Investigate differences.** Identify and research any discrepancies, timing differences, errors, omissions, or unexplained items.
- **5. Adjust.** Record adjusting entries to correct genuine errors.
- **6. Review and sign off.** A reviewer approves the reconciliation, and it is documented for audit.


## **Which accounts to reconcile**


- **Cash and bank accounts.** Reconciled to bank statements, the most frequent reconciliation. See[bank reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/automate-bank-reconciliation) .
- **Accounts receivable.** Reconciled to the AR subledger and aging.
- **Accounts payable.** Reconciled to the AP subledger.
- **Prepaid expenses and accruals.** Reconciled to supporting schedules.
- **Fixed assets.** Reconciled to the fixed-asset register and depreciation schedules.
- **Debt and intercompany.** Reconciled to loan statements and intercompany records.


## **Common pitfalls**


- **Leaving unexplained differences.** Plugging or carrying forward differences instead of investigating them, a classic source of errors that compound.
- **Reconciling only cash.** Cash gets reconciled religiously while accruals and prepaids are neglected.
- **Weak documentation.** Reconciliations that are not clearly supported and reviewed fail under audit.
- **Doing it all at period-end.** Batching every reconciliation into the close crunch instead of spreading the work.


## **How AI agents automate balance sheet reconciliation**

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is balance sheet reconciliation?**


Balance sheet reconciliation is the process of verifying that every balance-sheet account in the general ledger agrees with independent supporting evidence, bank statements, subledgers, and schedules, and investigating and correcting any differences. It is a core part of the close and a key internal control.


### **How do you reconcile the balance sheet?**


For each account: pull the GL balance, gather supporting evidence, compare and match the detail, investigate any differences, record adjusting entries for genuine errors, and have a reviewer sign off. Document each reconciliation for audit.


### **What is the difference between balance sheet reconciliation and account reconciliation?**


Account reconciliation is the general practice of reconciling any account. Balance sheet reconciliation specifically means reconciling the balance-sheet accounts (assets, liabilities, and equity) as a group, the heart of the month-end close. Bank reconciliation is one type within it.


### **Can balance sheet reconciliation be automated?**


Yes. AI agents can connect to the general ledger and supporting sources, match the detail, investigate discrepancies, and draft adjusting entries, with every match traceable to source and a human approving, turning it into a continuous process rather than an end-of-period task.


## **The bottom line**


Balance sheet reconciliation is how a company proves its balance sheet is right: every account tied to independent evidence, every difference investigated and resolved. It covers cash, receivables, payables, accruals, fixed assets, and more, and it is a core control in the close. The clearest shift in 2026 is AI agents that run it continuously, with every match traceable and a human approving.
